coding_guidelines:
Coding Guidelines — Key Principles
1. Specificity Rules
Always code to the highest level of specificity documented
"Pneumonia" alone → J18.9, but "E. coli pneumonia" → J15.5
Never assume specificity not documented (e.g., don't assume laterality)
2. Present on Admission (POA)
Conditions present at admission: POA = Y
Conditions developing during stay: POA = N
"Acute on chronic" — acute component may be POA=Y if present at admission
When documentation is unclear: POA = U (clinically undetermined)
3. Principal Diagnosis Selection
The condition established AFTER STUDY that caused the admission
Not always the same as the admitting diagnosis
For procedures: the condition that led to the procedure
4. Combination Codes
Some conditions have combination codes (disease + manifestation)
E11.65 = Type 2 DM with hyperglycemia (don't code separately)
I50.22 = Chronic systolic HF, acute exacerbation (single code captures both)
5. Sequencing
Principal diagnosis first
Complications and comorbidities (CC/MCC) as secondary
External cause codes for injuries
POA indicator on each diagnosis
6. Query Opportunities
When documentation is ambiguous, these are common query scenarios:
"Acute kidney injury" vs "Acute on chronic kidney disease"
"Respiratory failure" (type not specified — hypoxic vs hypercapnic?)
"Sepsis" vs "Severe sepsis" vs "Septic shock" (severity unclear)
"Heart failure" (systolic vs diastolic? acute vs chronic?)
Clinical significance of abnormal findings (e.g., is the hyponatremia clinically relevant?)
tool_call_specification:
Tool Call Specification
When the extraction system needs to look up a code, it should call the coding tool with:
ICD-10 Lookup Function:
Function: lookup_icd10
Parameters:
- clinical_term: string (the diagnosis description from the note)
- context: string (additional clinical information)
Returns:
- codes: array of {code, description, confidence}
- coding_guidance: string
CPT Lookup Function:
Function: lookup_cpt
Parameters:
- procedure_description: string (the procedure as documented)
- approach: string (open, laparoscopic, percutaneous, endoscopic)
- additional_details: string (laterality, complexity)
Returns:
- codes: array of {code, description, confidence}
- modifier_suggestions: array of strings
general_extraction_guidelines:
General Extraction Guidelines
Handling Ambiguity
If a measure element is not explicitly documented, mark as "Not documented" rather than inferring
If timing is unclear, extract whatever time references exist and flag for human review
If contradictory information exists between notes, extract both with sources noted
If shorthand is used (e.g., "cultures sent" without specifying which), extract as-is and flag
Confidence Scoring
For each extracted element, assign:
HIGH confidence: Explicitly stated, unambiguous (e.g., "Enoxaparin 40mg SubQ daily ordered at 14:30")
MEDIUM confidence: Implied or partially documented (e.g., "DVT prophylaxis per protocol" without specifying which drug)
LOW confidence: Inferred from context, ambiguous, or potentially conflicting (e.g., determining time-zero from narrative description)
PHI Elements to Identify (for redaction)
These elements are PHI and must be detected before external API processing:
Patient name
Date of birth
Medical record number (MRN)
Dates of service (dates can be shifted rather than removed)
Geographic data (addresses, zip codes)
Phone/fax numbers
Social Security Numbers
Provider names (depending on use case)
